decision_conditions: <p>Within 6 months of the date of this decision, evidence in the form of photographs and associated invoices for the work, shall be provided to the local planning authority for approval in writing demonstrating that the kitchen and all fittings have been removed from the outbuilding.&nbsp;</p><p>REASON: To ensure the outbuilding is not used as a separate residential unit and to protect the amenities of adjoining neighbours.&nbsp;</p>

<p><span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">Upon completion of the full scheme of planting works required under condition 2, by the end of June 2027, a compliance report from a suitably qualified arboriculturist must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. This report shall be accompanied by photographic evidence taken at the time of planting clearly showing the established new trees on site.</span></p><p><span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">REASON: To make good the loss of or damage to trees resulting from the unauthorised development, ensuring that the visual amenity and biodiversity value of the site and locality is protected and enhanced.</span><span style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;"></span></p>

<p style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">Within the next immediately available planting season (which runs from end October to end March) following the date of this decision, the applicant shall plant and establish two new trees on the site to mitigate the loss or damage to retained trees and/or trees on adjacent land caused by the unauthorised development.</p><p style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">The specific details of the tree planting scheme, including species, size, and precise location, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority prior to planting and within 6 months of the date of this permission. The submission must confirm that the trees will adhere to the following minimum standards:</p><ul style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;"><li style="margin-left: 15px;"><p><b>Size:</b>&nbsp;Each tree shall be at least light standard size (6-8 cm girth) as per BS 3936-1:1992).</p></li><li style="margin-left: 15px;"><p><b>Species:</b>&nbsp;The species must be native or those known to provide benefits to local wildlife and must not be considered invasive in Hackney.</p></li><li style="margin-left: 15px;"><p><b>Maintenance and Replacement:</b>&nbsp;The trees shall be maintained for a period of 10 years after planting. Should either tree be removed, die, be severely damaged, or become seriously diseased within this ten-year period, it shall be replaced during the next planting season with another tree as originally required to be planted by this condition, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.</p></li></ul><p style="color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: small;">REASON: To make good the loss of or damage to trees resulting from the unauthorised development, ensuring that the visual amenity and biodiversity value of the site and locality is protected and enhanced.</p>

<p><span style="background-color: transparent; color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 14px;">Within 3 months of the date of this planning permission, a&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; font-size: 14px; font-family: Arial;">detailed specification, a drainage layout and a management &amp; maintenance plan for at least one suitable sustainable drainage system (i.e. water butt with overflow, raingarden, bioretention planter box, living roof (substrate depth of 80 - 150mm excluding the vegetative mat), permeable paving etc.) shall be submitted to, and approved by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. If soakaways i.e. plastic modules and soakaway rings are used, an infiltration test must be carried out to ensure that the capacity of the soil is suitable for infiltration. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface water flow being discharged off-site and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume. The approved sustainable drainage system shall be implemented within 3 months of approval and maintained thereafter in accordance with the approved documents.</span></p><p>REASON: To ensure adequate drainage of the site and to prevent surface water flooding.</p>
description: Retrospective application for outbuilding to the rear garden
